points: Q3 results will show whether global RevPAR is tracking toward the raised 3–3.5% full-year guidance after Q2’s 3.4% print and 5% U.S. & Canada growth; reports suggest the key debate is whether that raised outlook can offset ongoing Middle East weakness.
The print will reveal if international demand stabilized from Q2’s 0.5% decline, with Europe, APEC and Greater China continuing to offset the Middle East drag.
Net room additions and the record ~629,000-room pipeline should feed franchise and base management fees; Q3 will show if conversion-driven signings keep fee growth in double digits.
The quarter will update capital-return pace after $1.1 billion of buybacks in Q2 and roughly $2.6 billion returned year-to-date through July 29, supporting EPS growth even if RevPAR moderates.
Q4 and FY1 setup depend on group and business travel broadening through the fall, while the 7% year-over-year pipeline expansion underpins FY2’s 12.4% consensus EPS growth.
With consensus FY1 EPS up 16.9% and FY2 up 12.4%, the long case needs Q3 adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS to keep pace so the premium PEG does not rest on stretched assumptions.
watch: Global RevPAR growth at or above the 3–3.5% full-year guidance — supports the long.
U.S. & Canada RevPAR holding near Q2’s 5% pace — supports the long.
International RevPAR improving from Q2’s -0.5% or at least not worsening — supports the long.
Franchise and base management fee growth staying in double digits — supports the long.
